newsitem.title: USA: Treasury selloff drags U.S. mortgage-backeds lower.
newsitem.headline: Treasury selloff drags U.S. mortgage-backeds lower.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were dragged down sharply by technically motivated selling in Treasuries on Thursday, market experts said.
Discount coupons suffered the greatest blow, sinking as low as 27/32 in 6.0 percent coupons.
"I haven't heard of anything other than the technicals today, and (traders) are going crazy with it," said one regional trader.
Pass-through yield spreads managed to tighten moderately against the 10-year Treasury note amid the brisk selloff, traders said.
"This is the norm," one trader said. "We tend to lag (Treasuries) in this type of trading."
By late afternoon Thursday, pass-throughs were 3/32 to 27/32 lower.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 7.5 percent coupons were off 23/32 at 100-17/32, yielding 123 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. The 10-year note was down 27/32 to yield 6.22 percent.
Fannie Mae 7.5 percent coupons were down 23/32 at 100-08/32, and Freddie Mac 7.5 percent coupons were off 20/32 at 100-16/32.
The sharp drop in pass-through prices may be ephemeral due to a possible pickup in prepayments later in the month, said one trader.
"If we get a pickup in prepayments down South and in the West, that will help us a lot," he said, explaining those regions tend to see more home sales during the winter months.
"The beauty ... of reinvesting cash is rolling back in," he said.
